title: An Adaptive Asynchronous Approach for the Single-Source Shortest Paths Problem
problem: Single-source shortest paths (SSSP) on large-scale graphs with billions to trillions of vertices and edges experiences large synchronization costs in bulk-synchronous algorithms like ∆-stepping. Asynchronous approaches reduce synchronization but suffer from wasteful speculative execution.
motivation: Efficient SSSP computation at extreme scale is essential for processing massive graphs on distributed systems with many nodes.
method: It coordinates work across multiple processors using messages and independently schedulable tasks to enable highly asynchronous execution without waiting for synchronization. It reduces wasted speculative work by adapting how much data it groups together at once and using evolving time windows to prioritize which graph connections (edges) to process first.
key_novelty: It continuously monitors parallel execution and adjusts how asynchronously the algorithm runs to balance the benefit of doing many things at once against the cost of wasted speculative work.
contributions: ACIC framework combining asynchronous execution with adaptive feedback mechanisms
Message-driven concurrent reductions and broadcasts for distributed SSSP
Evolving windows and prioritized edge relaxation flow techniques
Demonstration of scalability improvements over synchronous approaches
limitations: Results are preliminary with limited concrete performance metrics discussed.
